name: Why does the Front Range and foothills climate affect cabin interior sealing?

mainEntity.name: Why does the Front Range and foothills climate affect cabin interior sealing?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Denver and nearby foothills communities like Golden, Larkspur, and Sedalia, extreme seasonal humidity swings create dramatic expansion and contraction in interior logs. Heated winter air dries out timbers, causing them to shrink and pull away from rigid materials, while summer introduces brief humidity spikes. Standard non-elastic sealers quickly pull apart in this climate. Cabins in these areas require high-grade elastomeric compounds that maintain flexibility through rapid freeze-thaw cycles and intense low-humidity periods, preventing drafts from breaking through during harsh winter cold snaps.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low winter humidity and seasonal temperature swings cause Front Range cabin logs to shrink and expand, requiring elastomeric sealers that flex without cracking.
